_note: Additions from a Japan / Tokyo perspective, suggested by Qanta Shimizu (BASSDRUM). 'events_additions' items are ready to append to the 'events' array in public/events.json. 'tools_additions' entries are ready to merge into the 'tools' object in public/creative-code-data.json. All layers/categories use the existing fixed sets — no config change needed.

events_additions.title: IAMAS founded (Ogaki, Gifu)
events_additions.description: Institute of Advanced Media Arts and Sciences — Japan's counterpart to ITP. A small graduate school in Gifu prefecture that trained a generation of Japanese media artists, device-art makers, and creative technologists.

events_additions.title: Japan Media Arts Festival begins
events_additions.description: Annual festival run by Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, spanning art, entertainment, animation, and manga. For 25 years it was the main national showcase and archive for Japanese media art, awarding early work by teamLab, Rhizomatiks, and many others. Discontinued after its 25th edition.

events_additions.title: Maywa Denki formed
events_additions.description: Art unit styled as a small-town electrical company, led by Novmichi Tosa. Their absurdist 'nonsense machines' and mass-produced art products defined the Japanese 'device art' lineage — physical computing as performance and satire, long before the maker movement.

events_additions.title: Dumb Type — S/N
events_additions.description: Kyoto collective Dumb Type's landmark multimedia performance fusing synchronized video, sound, and staging with themes of sexuality, identity, and HIV/AIDS. A key bridge between performing arts and media technology in Asia, influencing figures like Ryoji Ikeda who worked within the collective.

events_additions.title: teamLab founded (Tokyo)
events_additions.description: Interdisciplinary 'ultratechnologists' collective founded by Toshiyuki Inoko and university friends. Grew from web production into one of the world's largest digital-art operations, culminating in the permanent museums already on this timeline (Borderless, 2018).

events_additions.title: Rhizomatiks founded (Tokyo)
events_additions.description: Studio founded by Seiichi Saito, Daito Manabe, and Motoi Ishibashi. Became the reference point for Japanese creative technology in the 2010s — stage tech for Perfume and Björk, drone performances (ELEVENPLAY), and research-grade R&D inside a commercial studio.

events_additions.title: Niconico (Nico Nico Douga) launches
events_additions.description: Japanese video platform with real-time comments overlaid on the video itself. Its remix culture (VOCALOID songs, MikuMikuDance, 'tried to make ___' maker videos) became a massive engine of collaborative creative-tech output outside the Western web.

events_additions.title: Daito Manabe — electric stimulus to face
events_additions.description: Face-hacking experiment using myoelectric sensors and electrical stimulation to make facial muscles twitch in sync with music. The viral video became a defining image of Japanese creative tech's DIY, body-hacking sensibility.

events_additions.title: wonderfl build flash online launches
events_additions.description: Browser-based Flash/ActionScript coding community by Kayac (Kamakura, Japan): write AS3 in the browser, see it compile live, and fork anyone else's code. A hub of the late Flash era's global creative-coding exchange, with a heavily Japanese user base.

events_additions.title: First SIGGRAPH Asia (Singapore)
events_additions.description: ACM SIGGRAPH's Asian edition, rotating through Singapore, Yokohama, Tokyo, Seoul, and other cities — institutionalizing the Asia-Pacific graphics and interactive-art community.

events_additions.title: Perfume Global Site Project — open motion data
events_additions.description: J-pop trio Perfume (with Rhizomatiks / Daito Manabe) released the group's motion-capture data and a music sample for free remixing, spawning a worldwide wave of fan-made visualizations. A rare case of a major-label pop act open-sourcing itself to the creative-coding community.

events_additions.title: Media Ambition Tokyo begins
events_additions.description: Annual city-wide showcase of experimental technology art across Tokyo venues (centered on Roppongi Hills), presenting work by teamLab, Rhizomatiks, and emerging Japanese artists.

ARToolKit.description: Marker-based augmented reality tracking library — the ancestor of consumer AR

releases.notes: Developed by Hirokazu Kato (Japan) with Mark Billinghurst at the HIT Lab. Square-marker camera tracking made AR possible on ordinary PCs and webcams.
Open-sourced via the HIT Lab, becoming the foundation for a decade of AR research and art projects.
Saqoosha's ActionScript 3 port brought marker-based AR into the browser via Flash, powering the late-2000s wave of web AR campaigns — a landmark of the Japanese Flash community.

VOCALOID.description: Yamaha's singing-voice synthesizer, catalyst of a massive UGC music culture

releases.notes: First commercial releases of Yamaha's singing synthesis engine.

Crypton Future Media's character voicebank triggered an unprecedented wave of user-generated music, animation (MikuMikuDance), and live concerts by a virtual performer — arguably the largest collaborative creative-tech phenomenon to emerge from Japan.
